clauses.mechanism: termination of the National War Labor Board by EO 9672 sec. 4 (parent body ended; no effective-date wording, read as effective on signing)
clauses.reason: item 1: Executive Order No. 9017 is amended by increasing the number of public members of the National War Labor Board from four to eight, with not more than four voting on any one matter. The clause continues, amended, as long as the Board exists (owner ruling 2026-10-21). EO 9672 section 4 says of the Board that it "is hereby terminated" (printed 'and the National War Labor Board is hereby terminated.' across lines), with no effective-date wording, so the Board and the enlarged public membership ended on signing, December 31, 1945. Before and after: before the amendment the Board had four public members; after it, eight, until the Board ended.

clauses.mechanism: one_time_revocation_performed_on_signing_date (no effective-date wording; read as effective on signing)
clauses.reason: item 2: Executive Order No. 9038 of January 24, 1942 and Executive Order No. 9395-A of November 20, 1943 are "are hereby revoked" (printed 'are hereby revoked.' at the end of the item). The order states no effective date, so the revocations were performed on signing, April 4, 1945; the filing date, April 5, 1945, is not used. The command is exhausted by performance and both orders stay revoked.

research_rationale:
EO 9535 (signed April 4, 1945; F.R. Doc. 45-5541, filed April 5, 1945) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Item 1 amends EO 9017 of January 12, 1942 (the National War Labor Board) by increasing the public members from four to eight, with not more than four voting on any one matter; item 2 revokes EO 9038 of January 24, 1942 (associate members) and EO 9395-A of November 20, 1943 (alternate public members). The held text then prints a Bureau of Customs regulation (T.D. 51214); it is another document and was not used. Item 2 is a one-time revocation performed on signing, 1945-04-04. Item 1 continues, amended, until its parent ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21); the National War Labor Board ended when EO 9672 (signed December 31, 1945; 11 FR 221) section 4 terminated it, with no effective-date wording, so on 1945-12-31. The whole-order end is the later date. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

savings.reason: EO 9672 section 4 transfers the personnel, records, property, funds and outstanding obligations of the National War Labor Board to the National Wage Stabilization Board in the Department of Labor; the public-member clause itself is not carried over, but the Board's functions and records are.
